Hyperinflation is an extreme increase in the general price level of goods and services in an economy. It occurs when the money supply grows faster than the economy can produce more goods and services, leading to prices rising dramatically.

When there is hyperinflation, it can cause widespread economic problems such as inflationary pressure on consumer spending, reduced purchasing power for citizens, and a decline in the value of financial assets like stocks and bonds. Hyperinflation can also have long-term effects on an economy, including increased social unrest, political instability, and even political collapse.

To prevent hyperinflation, governments typically implement monetary policy measures such as raising interest rates and controlling the money supply. They may also implement other economic policies to stabilize the economy, such as reducing government spending and increasing taxes.
